proofs.proof_tex:
For a Borel rule \(\delta\), define the clipped Borel rule
\[
 \bar\delta(z,y)=\operatorname{clip}(\delta(z,y)).
\]
We first verify the range of the causal target.  By \(\mathrm{def:local-target-mass}\), the cells \(\{z:z_{\Gamma_i}=x\}\), \(x\in X_i\), partition \(\Omega_n\).  Hence \(\mathrm{ass:target-product-policy}\) gives
\[
 \sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)
 =\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi'}(z)=1.
\]
Consequently, \(\mathrm{ass:bounded-schedules}\) and \(\mathrm{def:target-value}\) imply, for every \(v\in K\),
\[
 \lvert\theta(v)\rvert
 \le \frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}
 p_{\pi',i}(x)\lvert v_i(x)\rvert
 \le \frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}1=1.
\]
Projection onto \([-1,1]\) weakly decreases distance to every point of that interval.  Thus, pointwise in \((z,v)\),
\[
 \bigl(\bar\delta(z,N_zv)-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 \le
 \bigl(\delta(z,N_zv)-\theta(v)\bigr)^2.                                      \tag{1}
\]

Fix a genuine prior \(\nu\in\mathcal P(K)\) and let \(\mathbf V\sim\nu\).  Both \(\bar\delta(z,N_z\mathbf V)\) and \(\theta(\mathbf V)\) are bounded by one in absolute value.  Their conditional second moments therefore exist.  For each fixed \(z\), conditioning on \(N_z\mathbf V\) and expanding the square around the conditional mean gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\mathbb E_\nu\!\left[
 \bigl(\bar\delta(z,N_z\mathbf V)-\theta(\mathbf V)\bigr)^2
 \mid N_z\mathbf V\right]\\
 &\quad=
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu\!\left(\theta(\mathbf V)\mid N_z\mathbf V\right)
 +\left(
 \bar\delta(z,N_z\mathbf V)
 -\mathbb E_\nu[\theta(\mathbf V)\mid N_z\mathbf V]
 \right)^2\\
 &\quad\ge
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu\!\left(\theta(\mathbf V)\mid N_z\mathbf V\right).
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{2}
\]
No integrability assertion about the original, possibly unbounded, rule \(\delta\) is used.  Write
\[
 r_\eta(v)=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \bigl(\eta(z,N_zv)-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
\]
for either rule \(\eta\).  Inequality \((1)\), integration of the bounded loss of \(\bar\delta\), the fact that a supremum dominates a prior average, and \((2)\) yield, in this order,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{v\in K}r_\delta(v)
 &\ge \sup_{v\in K}r_{\bar\delta}(v)\\
 &\ge \int_K r_{\bar\delta}(v)\,d\nu(v)\\
 &=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \mathbb E_\nu\!\left[
 \bigl(\bar\delta(z,N_z\mathbf V)-\theta(\mathbf V)\bigr)^2\right]\\
 &\ge \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \mathbb E_\nu\!\left[
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu(\theta(\mathbf V)\mid N_z\mathbf V)\right]\\
 &=\mathcal B(\nu)=\operatorname{LB}(\nu),
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{3}
\]
where the first inequality remains valid in the extended nonnegative reals.  Taking the infimum of \((3)\) over all Borel \(\delta\) in \(\mathrm{def:unrestricted-frontier}\) proves
\[
 \operatorname{LB}(\nu)\le R^{\star}.                                           \tag{4}
\]

For every weight rule \(a\), the map \((z,y)\mapsto a_z^{\mathsf T}y\) is Borel.  It is therefore feasible for \(R^{\star}\), and \(\mathrm{def:linear-frontier}\) gives
\[
 R^{\star}
 \le \inf_a\sup_{v\in K}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 =F.                                                                              \tag{5}
\]
For a fixed feasible \(a\), \(\mathrm{def:linear-frontier}\) and \(\mathrm{def:primal-certificate}\) similarly give
\[
 F\le
 \sup_{v\in K}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 =\operatorname{UB}(a).                                                           \tag{6}
\]

Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\) supplies an attaining weight rule \(a^{\star}\).  Applying the projection inequality in \((1)\) with \(\delta(z,y)=(a_z^{\star})^{\mathsf T}y\), then using \(\mathrm{def:clipped-incidence-estimator}\), gives
\[
 \sup_{v\in K}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{inc}}(z,N_zv)-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 \le
 \sup_{v\in K}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \bigl((a_z^{\star})^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 =F.                                                                              \tag{7}
\]
Equations \((4)\)--\((7)\) prove all assertions.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every admissible fixed instance, write \(\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\) for the vertex set of the local polytope \(K_i\).  The exact linear frontier is the finite convex epigraph program
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F={}&\min_{\substack{t\in\mathbb R\\ a\in(\mathbb R^{V_n})^{\Omega_n}}}t\\
 \text{subject to }{}&
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \left[
 \sum_{i\in V_n}(a_z)_i v_i(z_{\Gamma_i})
 -\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)v_i(x)
 \right]^2\le t
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\prod_{i\in V_n}\operatorname{vert}(K_i).
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{P}
\]
Its explicit numeric inputs are the tables \(p_\pi(z)\), \(p_{\pi',i}(x)\), the restrictions \(z_{\Gamma_i}\), and the vertex-evaluation tables \(\{(v_i(x))_{x\in X_i}:v_i\in\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\}\), all computed from the known \(\pi,\pi',\Gamma_i,\mathcal S_i\).  Program \((P)\) has exactly \(n2^n+1\) real decision variables and \(\prod_{i\in V_n}\lvert\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\rvert\) listed convex quadratic constraints.  An optimum exists, its weight component may be taken to be \(a^{\star}\), and there is a matching moment certificate \(M\in\mathfrak M(K)\) such that
\[
 F=\mathcal D=
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)\psi_z(M).                                         \tag{D}
\]
When \(F>0\), \(M\) may be chosen to be the minimum-rank optimizer \(M^{\star}\) from \(\mathrm{def:adaptive-rank-fiber-complexity}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For a fixed weight array \(a\), put
\[
 Q_a(v)=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2.
\]
Each residual in this sum is linear in \(v\).  Since \(s\mapsto s^2\) is convex and the design masses are nonnegative, for \(v,w\in K\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Q_a(\lambda v+(1-\lambda)w)
 \le \lambda Q_a(v)+(1-\lambda)Q_a(w).                                           \tag{8}
\]

We next justify the vertex reduction rather than assume it.  By \(\mathrm{def:local-evaluation-polytope}\), \(K_i\) is the intersection of the finite-dimensional space \(H_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{X_i}\) with the finitely many slabs \(-1\le h(x)\le1\), \(x\in X_i\).  It contains zero, is closed, and is bounded in the evaluation coordinates; hence it is a nonempty compact polytope.  Every point of such a polytope is a convex combination of its vertices: indeed, induct on the dimension of the point's smallest face.  A zero-dimensional face is a vertex.  In a positive-dimensional smallest face, a line through the point in a nonzero direction of the face meets the compact face in a closed segment with two boundary endpoints; the point is a convex combination of those endpoints, and each endpoint has a smallest face of strictly smaller dimension.  The induction terminates because the dimension is finite.  This also shows that the vertex set is finite, since every vertex is the unique solution of a full-rank subsystem selected from finitely many defining equalities.

Thus write each \(v_i\in K_i\) as \(v_i=\sum_{k_i}\lambda_{i,k_i}u_{i,k_i}\), where \(u_{i,k_i}\in\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\), \(\lambda_{i,k_i}\ge0\), and \(\sum_{k_i}\lambda_{i,k_i}=1\).  Expanding the product gives
\[
 v=\sum_{(k_i)_{i\in V_n}}
 \left(\prod_{i\in V_n}\lambda_{i,k_i}\right)
 (u_{i,k_i})_{i\in V_n},                                                         \tag{9}
\]
a convex combination of the product vertices.  Applying the two-point convexity inequality \((8)\) repeatedly to the finite combination \((9)\) yields
\[
 \sup_{v\in K}Q_a(v)
 =\max_{v\in\prod_i\operatorname{vert}(K_i)}Q_a(v).                              \tag{10}
\]
The left-to-right inequality in \((10)\) follows from the convex combination; the reverse inequality follows because every listed product vertex belongs to \(K\).

By \(\mathrm{def:observation-operator}\) and \(\mathrm{def:target-value}\), the residual at a product vertex is exactly
\[
 a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)
 =\sum_{i\in V_n}(a_z)_iv_i(z_{\Gamma_i})
 -\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)v_i(x).                    \tag{11}
\]
Substituting \((10)\) and \((11)\) into \(\mathrm{def:linear-frontier}\) gives precisely the epigraph program \((P)\).  There are \(2^n\) vectors \(a_z\in\mathbb R^{V_n}\) and one scalar \(t\), hence \(n2^n+1\) real variables.  Equation \((10)\) supplies one listed constraint for each element of \(\prod_i\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\), hence the claimed product count.  Each constraint is a nonnegative weighted sum of squares of affine functions of \(a\), bounded above by the affine variable \(t\); it is therefore convex quadratic.  The input list in the statement is exactly the list of coefficients occurring in \((11)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\), the infimum over \(a\) is attained, so the epigraph optimum is attained with \(t=F\) and weight component \(a^{\star}\).

It remains to certify the matching dual optimizer.  For \(M\in\mathfrak M(K)\), the range condition in \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\) and completion of the positive-semidefinite quadratic give, for every \(z\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \psi_z(M)
 &=\min_{b\in\mathbb R^{V_n}}
 \langle\ell-N_z^{\ast}b,\,M(\ell-N_z^{\ast}b)\rangle_E.
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{12}
\]
To check \((12)\), expand the right side as
\[
 \langle\ell,M\ell\rangle_E
 -2\langle b,N_zM\ell\rangle_{V_n}
 +\langle b,(N_zMN_z^{\ast})b\rangle_{V_n}.
\]
Because \(N_zM\ell\) lies in the range of \(N_zMN_z^{\ast}\), its minimizers solve the normal equation and the minimum is
\[
 \langle\ell,M\ell\rangle_E
 -\left\langle N_zM\ell,
 (N_zMN_z^{\ast})^{\dagger}N_zM\ell\right\rangle_{V_n},
\]
which is the defining formula for \(\psi_z(M)\).

Independence of the finitely many coordinates \(b_z\) in \((12)\) implies
\[
 \Phi(M):=\sum_zp_\pi(z)\psi_z(M)
 =\inf_{a}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \langle\ell-N_z^{\ast}a_z,\,M(\ell-N_z^{\ast}a_z)\rangle_E.                    \tag{13}
\]
For fixed \(a\), the expression after the infimum is continuous and affine in \(M\); hence \(\Phi\), an infimum of continuous affine functions, is upper semicontinuous.  The set \(K\) is compact by the preceding local argument and the finite product construction in \(\mathrm{def:bounded-fourier-class}\).  Therefore \(\{v\otimes v:v\in K\}\) is compact.  Its convex hull \(\mathfrak M(K)\) is compact as well.  To see this directly, let \(d\) be the dimension of the real vector space of self-adjoint operators on \(E\).  Any convex combination of more than \(d+1\) operators has affinely dependent support: there are coefficients, not all zero, whose sum and whose weighted operator sum are both zero.  Moving the mixture weights in that null direction until one first reaches zero preserves the represented operator and removes one support point.  Iteration represents every element of the convex hull using at most \(d+1\) support points.  Thus \(\mathfrak M(K)\) is the continuous image of the compact product of \(d+1\) copies of \(\{v\otimes v:v\in K\}\) and the compact \(d\)-simplex, and is compact.  The upper-semicontinuous function \(\Phi\) attains its maximum there, say at \(M^{\circ}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\) and the exact identity in \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\),
Indeed, a maximizing sequence has a convergent subsequence by compactness, and upper semicontinuity makes the limit's value at least the subsequential limit of the values.  Thus the asserted maximizer exists.  We then have
\[
 \Phi(M^{\circ})=\mathcal D=F,
\]
which is \((D)\).  If \(F>0\), the nonempty set of maximizers has a minimum integer rank, and \(\mathrm{def:adaptive-rank-fiber-complexity}\) names such a certificate \(M^{\star}\).  This completes the proof.

For the smallest exact stress test, take \(n=1\), \(\Gamma_1=\{1\}\), and \(\mathcal S_1=\{\varnothing,\{1\}\}\).  The two retained characters span all functions on \(X_1=\{0,1\}\), so in evaluation coordinates \(K_1=[-1,1]^2\) and
\[
 \operatorname{vert}(K_1)=\{(-1,-1),(-1,1),(1,-1),(1,1)\}.
\]
There are the two assignments \(z=0,1\).  Program \((P)\) therefore has the three variables \((a_0,a_1,t)\), exactly \(1\cdot2^1+1\), and four listed constraints, exactly \(\lvert\operatorname{vert}(K_1)\rvert\).  For every fixed \((a_0,a_1)\), its risk is a convex quadratic on the square.  Expressing an arbitrary point of the square as the product mixture of its four corners and applying \((8)\) proves that none of the continuum of nonvertex schedules exceeds those four enumerated risks.  Thus exhaustive enumeration agrees with \((P)\) on the smallest nonconstant instance, including the variable and constraint counts.
added_lemmas.justification: The vertex epigraph turns the exact frontier into a directly implementable finite convex program and pairs its optimum with a checkable moment certificate.
added_lemmas.gap: The open bounded-treewidth question concerns compression of this program, not existence or exactness of the fully enumerated program itself.
added_lemmas.consumer: An analyst can enumerate the local-polytope vertices, solve the displayed program, and report matching primal weights and a moment-dual certificate.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every admissible fixed finite-population instance, the unrestricted and linear minimax risks obey the instance-adaptive certificate
\[
 \max\left\{\frac{F}{r_{\star}},m_{\mathrm{fib}}\right\}
 \le R^{\star}\le F=\mathcal D\le S_{\mathrm{fib}},
 \qquad
 \frac{F}{\kappa}\le R^{\star}\le F.                                            \tag{14}
\]
When \(F>0\), \(r_{\star}\) is the minimum rank of a dual optimizer; it has the stated value-one convention when \(F=0\).  The quantity \(\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\) is the effective number of assignment fibers carrying nonzero ambiguity.  When \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}>0\),
\[
 1\le\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}
 \le\left\lvert\{z\in\Omega_n:\rho_z>0\}\right\rvert
 \le2^n.
\]
When \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}=0\), all four values \(R^{\star},F,\mathcal D,S_{\mathrm{fib}}\) are zero.  The clipped incidence estimator has worst-case risk at most \(F\).  The factors in \((14)\) are instance dependent; no universal numerical comparison constant is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The declared lemma \(\mathrm{lem:rank-fiber-genuine-prior-certificates}\) supplies, for \(F>0\), a genuine prior with lower certificate \(F/r_{\star}\), and for every assignment fiber a genuine two-point prior with lower certificate at least \(p_\pi(z)\rho_z^2\).  Applying \(\mathrm{prop:primal-dual-certificates}\) to these priors gives
\[
 \max\left\{\frac{F}{r_{\star}},m_{\mathrm{fib}}\right\}\le R^{\star}.          \tag{15}
\]
The same lemma constructs, separately for every \(z\), a linear extension whose worst absolute error is \(\rho_z\); summing its squared errors with the design masses gives
\[
 F\le S_{\mathrm{fib}}.                                                           \tag{16}
\]
Moreover, \(\mathrm{prop:primal-dual-certificates}\) gives \(R^{\star}\le F\) and the clipped-estimator risk bound, while \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\) gives \(F=\mathcal D\).  Equations \((15)\) and \((16)\) establish the first chain in \((14)\).

When \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}>0\), the definition
\[
 \kappa=\min\{r_{\star},\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}=\frac{S_{\mathrm{fib}}}{m_{\mathrm{fib}}}
\]
allows two cases.  If \(\kappa=r_{\star}\), \((15)\) gives \(F/\kappa\le R^{\star}\).  If \(\kappa=\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\), then \((16)\) and the fiber lower bound give
\[
 \frac{F}{\kappa}
 \le\frac{S_{\mathrm{fib}}}{\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}}
 =m_{\mathrm{fib}}
 \le R^{\star}.
\]
The cardinality bound and the case \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}=0\), including the conclusion that every displayed risk is zero, are exactly the boundary conclusions of \(\mathrm{lem:rank-fiber-genuine-prior-certificates}\).  This proves every assertion and also makes explicit why the comparison factor is not dimension free.
added_lemmas.justification: The certificate quantifies the all-Borel value of the attainable linear risk through observable finite-instance rank and selector-fiber factors without asserting dimension-free equivalence.
added_lemmas.gap: ChenValiantValiant2020 leaves the universal comparison open; the proved conclusion is the exact unconditional comparison supplied by minimum dual rank and effective fiber count.
added_lemmas.consumer: Experimenters can report the incidence upper risk together with rank and fiber lower certificates that show how informative it is for unrestricted procedures.

added_lemmas.statement: As a rowwise corollary of the instance-adaptive risk certificate, let \(\mathfrak A\in\mathsf{Adm}\) and let \(r_n,\rho_{n,z},S_{n,\mathrm{fib}},m_{n,\mathrm{fib}},\kappa_{n,\mathrm{fib}}\), and \(\kappa_n\) be the quantities in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive-rank-fiber-complexity}\).  Then: \(\mathrm{(a)}\) \(F_n\to0\) implies \(R_n^{\star}\to0\); \(\mathrm{(b)}\) in every fixed row, \(R_n^{\star}=0\) if and only if \(F_n=0\); \(\mathrm{(c)}\) \(\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\to0\) implies \(F_n\to0\); and \(\mathrm{(d)}\) on every subfamily satisfying \(\sup_n\kappa_n<\infty\), one has \(R_n^{\star}\to0\) if and only if \(F_n\to0\).  Clause \(\mathrm{(d)}\) is conditional on that subfamily property and does not add a condition to \(\mathsf{Adm}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathfrak A\in\mathsf{Adm}\).  Applying \(\mathrm{thm:instance-adaptive-risk-certificate}\) to every row and using the rowwise definition of \(\kappa_n\) gives
\[
 0\le R_n^{\star}\le F_n\le\kappa_nR_n^{\star},
 \qquad n\ge1.                                                                    \tag{17}
\]
The factor \(\kappa_n\) is finite: if \(m_{n,\mathrm{fib}}=0\), it equals one by definition; otherwise the cardinality bound in the cited theorem gives \(\kappa_n\le\kappa_{n,\mathrm{fib}}\le2^n\).

If \(F_n\to0\), the first two inequalities in \((17)\) squeeze \(R_n^{\star}\) to zero, proving \(\mathrm{(a)}\).  In a fixed row, \(F_n=0\) implies \(R_n^{\star}=0\) by \(R_n^{\star}\le F_n\), while \(R_n^{\star}=0\) implies \(F_n=0\) by \(F_n\le\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\) and finiteness of \(\kappa_n\).  This proves \(\mathrm{(b)}\).

If \(\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\to0\), the last inequality in \((17)\) squeezes \(F_n\) to zero, proving \(\mathrm{(c)}\).  Finally, on a subfamily with \(C:=\sup_n\kappa_n<\infty\), \(R_n^{\star}\to0\) implies
\[
 0\le F_n\le\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\le C R_n^{\star}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{(a)}\), this proves the equivalence in \(\mathrm{(d)}\).  No reverse implication has been used or asserted when \(\kappa_n\) is unbounded.
added_lemmas.justification: This supporting proposition records the exact rowwise consistency consequences of the rank/fiber sandwich.
added_lemmas.gap: LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy gives a sufficient degree envelope and HarshawSavjeWang2022 treats the Riesz-estimator class; the reverse all-Borel implication here is explicitly restricted to uniformly bounded instance complexity.
added_lemmas.consumer: A vanishing linear frontier certifies unrestricted consistency on every admissible array, while bounded \(\kappa_n\) identifies subfamilies on which the converse is valid.

prose_updates.tldr: For the fixed causal target \(\theta\) under one known product-Bernoulli source assignment, the exact assignment-indexed linear minimax risk satisfies \(F=\mathcal D\), is attained, and is computable by an explicit vertex epigraph with \(n2^n+1\) variables and \(\prod_i|\operatorname{vert}(K_i)|\) constraints. Genuine-prior and primal certificates give \(\max\{F/r_{\star},m_{\mathrm{fib}}\}\le R^{\star}\le F\le S_{\mathrm{fib}}\), while the clipped incidence rule attains risk at most \(F\). Additive hubs have the exact one-hub all-Borel equality and the broader \(n^{-1}\) frontier; the Loomba--Eckles envelope is separated by \(\Theta_{\varepsilon}(n+n^2(q_n-p_n)^2)\), with elbow \(|q_n-p_n|\asymp n^{-1/2}\). Dimension-free linear-versus-all-Borel comparison and exact compressed bounded-treewidth computation remain open.

project_justification.gap: LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy supplies unbiased Fourier transport and a degree-envelope sufficient condition, while ChenValiantValiant2020 leaves the semilinear-versus-unrestricted universal gap open. Neither gives an exact biased linear frontier with a directly solvable finite program and genuine-prior lower certificates for heterogeneous off-policy network selectors.
project_justification.niche: The note treats fixed bounded local-Fourier schedules under known heterogeneous source and target product policies. Its finite-instance rank and selector-fiber geometry records information discarded by maximum dependency degree, while keeping assignment as the only source of randomness.
project_justification.fill: The contribution proves \(F=\mathcal D\), lifts the exact fully expanded vertex program with attaining primal and moment certificates, proves the instance-adaptive rank/fiber comparison and its supporting consistency corollary, and establishes the additive-hub \(n^{-1}\) frontier plus the Loomba--Eckles local-policy elbow. It does not claim the unresolved dimension-free comparison or compressed treewidth exactness.

prose_updates.related_work: LoombaEckles2026OffPolicy, Equation (4), Proposition 3.1, and Theorem 5.1 supply the policy-indexed Fourier transport comparator and the \(B_n^{\mathrm{LE}}(D_n^{\mathrm{LE}}+1)/n\) envelope that the hub results separate from the exact frontier. ChenValiantValiant2020, Theorem 1, Fact 1, Appendix D, and Section 4 gives the closest generic semilinear formulation, exhibits nonlinear improvement, and leaves the dimension-free gap open; the present theorem therefore reports instance-dependent rank and fiber factors rather than claiming a universal constant. BrownCohen2021 gives an all-estimator constant only under its non-expansion condition. DonohoLiuMacGibbon1990 concerns Gaussian quadratically convex experiments, not noiseless selectors. KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax studies conflict-graph minimax risk for contrastive network exposures rather than heterogeneous source-target Fourier transport. HarshawSavjeWang2022 characterizes consistency within the Riesz-estimator class; here the consistency statement is explicitly a corollary of the all-Borel rank/fiber sandwich. The accepted-bank result \(\texttt{exp\_snipe\_degree\_frontier/thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier}\) gives a unit-Bernoulli bounded-outcome, bounded-degree family rate; this note instead targets an off-policy average under heterogeneous source and target product laws on local-Fourier polytopes and proves a fixed-instance rank/fiber certificate rather than a degree-family frontier. WainwrightJordan2004 and PeyrardEtAl2019 motivate bounded-treewidth elimination only after locality is proved; the width-one obstruction here shows that raw incidence-bag moments omit the squared target moment. ChinEcklesUgander2022 and CreponEtAl2013 are prospective design-audit consumers once their design-specific inputs are supplied; no empirical reanalysis is claimed.
prose_updates.interpretation: The causal object is \(\theta(v)\), the target-policy finite-population average of fixed potential outcomes. The quantities \(F\), \(\mathcal D\), and \(R^{\star}\) are design-risk functionals for estimating that object from the single source-randomized assignment; they do not redefine it. The expanded program computes the best assignment-indexed linear rule, the moment optimizer certifies its value, and genuine priors calibrate what any Borel rule must lose. The rank and fiber factors quantify the remaining nonlinear advantage instance by instance. On additive hubs, signed probability-weighted incidence geometry retains an \(n^{-1}\) frontier even when the maximum-overlap envelope is order \(n\) or \(n^2(q_n-p_n)^2\) larger.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The proved expanded epigraph is exponential in the number of assignments and in the product of local vertex counts. Raw exposure-incidence treewidth does not localize the squared target moment even at width one, so an exact \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{in}})2^{O(w)}\) algorithm still requires a proved compressed global target-sum/separator state or a genuine complexity obstruction. The comparison factors \(r_{\star}\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\) can grow, so they do not settle the universal all-estimator constant, and reverse consistency is unconditional only after multiplication by \(\kappa_n\) or on subfamilies with bounded \(\kappa_n\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established results are the selector reduction, exact moment duality \(F=\mathcal D\), attainment, the fully expanded finite convex program, clipped-incidence and genuine-prior certificates, the instance-adaptive rank/fiber comparison, its complexity-calibrated consistency corollary, exact additive one-hub equality, the broader additive-hub \(n^{-1}\) rate and envelope elbow, and disjoint-motif recovery under its explicit unbiased-witness premise. No dimension-free comparison over all admissible arrays is claimed; no unconditional reverse-consistency theorem is claimed when \(\kappa_n\) diverges; and compressed bounded-treewidth exactness remains the stated open question. Extension to the full Loomba--Eckles exposure-action-order class, correlated or adaptive assignment, studentization, and empirical reanalysis of the Cr\'epon or Chin--Eckles--Ugander applications are outside the proved scope.

proofs.proof_tex:
For a Borel rule \(\delta\), define the clipped Borel rule
\[
 \bar\delta(z,y)=\operatorname{clip}(\delta(z,y)).
\]
We first verify the range of the causal target.  By \(\mathrm{def:local-target-mass}\), the cells \(\{z:z_{\Gamma_i}=x\}\), \(x\in X_i\), partition \(\Omega_n\).  Hence \(\mathrm{ass:target-product-policy}\) gives
\[
 \sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)
 =\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi'}(z)=1.
\]
Consequently, \(\mathrm{ass:bounded-schedules}\) and \(\mathrm{def:target-value}\) imply, for every \(v\in K\),
\[
 \lvert\theta(v)\rvert
 \le \frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}
 p_{\pi',i}(x)\lvert v_i(x)\rvert
 \le \frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}1=1.
\]
Projection onto \([-1,1]\) weakly decreases distance to every point of that interval.  Thus, pointwise in \((z,v)\),
\[
 \bigl(\bar\delta(z,N_zv)-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 \le
 \bigl(\delta(z,N_zv)-\theta(v)\bigr)^2.                                      \tag{1}
\]

Fix a genuine prior \(\nu\in\mathcal P(K)\) and let \(\mathbf V\sim\nu\).  Both \(\bar\delta(z,N_z\mathbf V)\) and \(\theta(\mathbf V)\) are bounded by one in absolute value.  Their conditional second moments therefore exist.  For each fixed \(z\), conditioning on \(N_z\mathbf V\) and expanding the square around the conditional mean gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\mathbb E_\nu\!\left[
 \bigl(\bar\delta(z,N_z\mathbf V)-\theta(\mathbf V)\bigr)^2
 \mid N_z\mathbf V\right]\\
 &\quad=
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu\!\left(\theta(\mathbf V)\mid N_z\mathbf V\right)
 +\left(
 \bar\delta(z,N_z\mathbf V)
 -\mathbb E_\nu[\theta(\mathbf V)\mid N_z\mathbf V]
 \right)^2\\
 &\quad\ge
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu\!\left(\theta(\mathbf V)\mid N_z\mathbf V\right).
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{2}
\]
No integrability assertion about the original, possibly unbounded, rule \(\delta\) is used.  Write
\[
 r_\eta(v)=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \bigl(\eta(z,N_zv)-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
\]
for either rule \(\eta\).  Inequality \((1)\), integration of the bounded loss of \(\bar\delta\), the fact that a supremum dominates a prior average, and \((2)\) yield, in this order,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{v\in K}r_\delta(v)
 &\ge \sup_{v\in K}r_{\bar\delta}(v)\\
 &\ge \int_K r_{\bar\delta}(v)\,d\nu(v)\\
 &=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \mathbb E_\nu\!\left[
 \bigl(\bar\delta(z,N_z\mathbf V)-\theta(\mathbf V)\bigr)^2\right]\\
 &\ge \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \mathbb E_\nu\!\left[
 \operatorname{Var}_\nu(\theta(\mathbf V)\mid N_z\mathbf V)\right]\\
 &=\mathcal B(\nu)=\operatorname{LB}(\nu),
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{3}
\]
where the first inequality remains valid in the extended nonnegative reals.  Taking the infimum of \((3)\) over all Borel \(\delta\) in \(\mathrm{def:unrestricted-frontier}\) proves
\[
 \operatorname{LB}(\nu)\le R^{\star}.                                           \tag{4}
\]

For every weight rule \(a\), the map \((z,y)\mapsto a_z^{\mathsf T}y\) is Borel.  It is therefore feasible for \(R^{\star}\), and \(\mathrm{def:linear-frontier}\) gives
\[
 R^{\star}
 \le \inf_a\sup_{v\in K}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 =F.                                                                              \tag{5}
\]
For a fixed feasible \(a\), \(\mathrm{def:linear-frontier}\) and \(\mathrm{def:primal-certificate}\) similarly give
\[
 F\le
 \sup_{v\in K}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 =\operatorname{UB}(a).                                                           \tag{6}
\]

Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\) supplies an attaining weight rule \(a^{\star}\).  Applying the projection inequality in \((1)\) with \(\delta(z,y)=(a_z^{\star})^{\mathsf T}y\), then using \(\mathrm{def:clipped-incidence-estimator}\), gives
\[
 \sup_{v\in K}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \bigl(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{inc}}(z,N_zv)-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 \le
 \sup_{v\in K}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \bigl((a_z^{\star})^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2
 =F.                                                                              \tag{7}
\]
Equations \((4)\)--\((7)\) prove all assertions.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every admissible fixed instance, write \(\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\) for the vertex set of the local polytope \(K_i\).  The exact linear frontier is the finite convex epigraph program
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F={}&\min_{\substack{t\in\mathbb R\\ a\in(\mathbb R^{V_n})^{\Omega_n}}}t\\
 \text{subject to }{}&
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \left[
 \sum_{i\in V_n}(a_z)_i v_i(z_{\Gamma_i})
 -\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)v_i(x)
 \right]^2\le t
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\prod_{i\in V_n}\operatorname{vert}(K_i).
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{P}
\]
Its explicit numeric inputs are the tables \(p_\pi(z)\), \(p_{\pi',i}(x)\), the restrictions \(z_{\Gamma_i}\), and the vertex-evaluation tables \(\{(v_i(x))_{x\in X_i}:v_i\in\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\}\), all computed from the known \(\pi,\pi',\Gamma_i,\mathcal S_i\).  Program \((P)\) has exactly \(n2^n+1\) real decision variables and \(\prod_{i\in V_n}\lvert\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\rvert\) listed convex quadratic constraints.  An optimum exists, its weight component may be taken to be \(a^{\star}\), and there is a matching moment certificate \(M\in\mathfrak M(K)\) such that
\[
 F=\mathcal D=
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)\psi_z(M).                                         \tag{D}
\]
When \(F>0\), \(M\) may be chosen to be the minimum-rank optimizer \(M^{\star}\) from \(\mathrm{def:adaptive-rank-fiber-complexity}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For a fixed weight array \(a\), put
\[
 Q_a(v)=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2.
\]
Each residual in this sum is linear in \(v\).  Since \(s\mapsto s^2\) is convex and the design masses are nonnegative, for \(v,w\in K\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Q_a(\lambda v+(1-\lambda)w)
 \le \lambda Q_a(v)+(1-\lambda)Q_a(w).                                           \tag{8}
\]

We next justify the vertex reduction rather than assume it.  By \(\mathrm{def:local-evaluation-polytope}\), \(K_i\) is the intersection of the finite-dimensional space \(H_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{X_i}\) with the finitely many slabs \(-1\le h(x)\le1\), \(x\in X_i\).  It contains zero, is closed, and is bounded in the evaluation coordinates; hence it is a nonempty compact polytope.  Every point of such a polytope is a convex combination of its vertices: indeed, induct on the dimension of the point's smallest face.  A zero-dimensional face is a vertex.  In a positive-dimensional smallest face, a line through the point in a nonzero direction of the face meets the compact face in a closed segment with two boundary endpoints; the point is a convex combination of those endpoints, and each endpoint has a smallest face of strictly smaller dimension.  The induction terminates because the dimension is finite.  This also shows that the vertex set is finite, since every vertex is the unique solution of a full-rank subsystem selected from finitely many defining equalities.

Thus write each \(v_i\in K_i\) as \(v_i=\sum_{k_i}\lambda_{i,k_i}u_{i,k_i}\), where \(u_{i,k_i}\in\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\), \(\lambda_{i,k_i}\ge0\), and \(\sum_{k_i}\lambda_{i,k_i}=1\).  Expanding the product gives
\[
 v=\sum_{(k_i)_{i\in V_n}}
 \left(\prod_{i\in V_n}\lambda_{i,k_i}\right)
 (u_{i,k_i})_{i\in V_n},                                                         \tag{9}
\]
a convex combination of the product vertices.  Applying the two-point convexity inequality \((8)\) repeatedly to the finite combination \((9)\) yields
\[
 \sup_{v\in K}Q_a(v)
 =\max_{v\in\prod_i\operatorname{vert}(K_i)}Q_a(v).                              \tag{10}
\]
The left-to-right inequality in \((10)\) follows from the convex combination; the reverse inequality follows because every listed product vertex belongs to \(K\).

By \(\mathrm{def:observation-operator}\) and \(\mathrm{def:target-value}\), the residual at a product vertex is exactly
\[
 a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)
 =\sum_{i\in V_n}(a_z)_iv_i(z_{\Gamma_i})
 -\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)v_i(x).                    \tag{11}
\]
Substituting \((10)\) and \((11)\) into \(\mathrm{def:linear-frontier}\) gives precisely the epigraph program \((P)\).  There are \(2^n\) vectors \(a_z\in\mathbb R^{V_n}\) and one scalar \(t\), hence \(n2^n+1\) real variables.  Equation \((10)\) supplies one listed constraint for each element of \(\prod_i\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\), hence the claimed product count.  Each constraint is a nonnegative weighted sum of squares of affine functions of \(a\), bounded above by the affine variable \(t\); it is therefore convex quadratic.  The input list in the statement is exactly the list of coefficients occurring in \((11)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\), the infimum over \(a\) is attained, so the epigraph optimum is attained with \(t=F\) and weight component \(a^{\star}\).

It remains to certify the matching dual optimizer.  For \(M\in\mathfrak M(K)\), the range condition in \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\) and completion of the positive-semidefinite quadratic give, for every \(z\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \psi_z(M)
 &=\min_{b\in\mathbb R^{V_n}}
 \langle\ell-N_z^{\ast}b,\,M(\ell-N_z^{\ast}b)\rangle_E.
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{12}
\]
To check \((12)\), expand the right side as
\[
 \langle\ell,M\ell\rangle_E
 -2\langle b,N_zM\ell\rangle_{V_n}
 +\langle b,(N_zMN_z^{\ast})b\rangle_{V_n}.
\]
Because \(N_zM\ell\) lies in the range of \(N_zMN_z^{\ast}\), its minimizers solve the normal equation and the minimum is
\[
 \langle\ell,M\ell\rangle_E
 -\left\langle N_zM\ell,
 (N_zMN_z^{\ast})^{\dagger}N_zM\ell\right\rangle_{V_n},
\]
which is the defining formula for \(\psi_z(M)\).

Independence of the finitely many coordinates \(b_z\) in \((12)\) implies
\[
 \Phi(M):=\sum_zp_\pi(z)\psi_z(M)
 =\inf_{a}\sum_zp_\pi(z)
 \langle\ell-N_z^{\ast}a_z,\,M(\ell-N_z^{\ast}a_z)\rangle_E.                    \tag{13}
\]
For fixed \(a\), the expression after the infimum is continuous and affine in \(M\); hence \(\Phi\), an infimum of continuous affine functions, is upper semicontinuous.  The set \(K\) is compact by the preceding local argument and the finite product construction in \(\mathrm{def:bounded-fourier-class}\).  Therefore \(\{v\otimes v:v\in K\}\) is compact.  Its convex hull \(\mathfrak M(K)\) is compact as well.  To see this directly, let \(d\) be the dimension of the real vector space of self-adjoint operators on \(E\).  Any convex combination of more than \(d+1\) operators has affinely dependent support: there are coefficients, not all zero, whose sum and whose weighted operator sum are both zero.  Moving the mixture weights in that null direction until one first reaches zero preserves the represented operator and removes one support point.  Iteration represents every element of the convex hull using at most \(d+1\) support points.  Thus \(\mathfrak M(K)\) is the continuous image of the compact product of \(d+1\) copies of \(\{v\otimes v:v\in K\}\) and the compact \(d\)-simplex, and is compact.  The upper-semicontinuous function \(\Phi\) attains its maximum there, say at \(M^{\circ}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\) and the exact identity in \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\),
Indeed, a maximizing sequence has a convergent subsequence by compactness, and upper semicontinuity makes the limit's value at least the subsequential limit of the values.  Thus the asserted maximizer exists.  We then have
\[
 \Phi(M^{\circ})=\mathcal D=F,
\]
which is \((D)\).  If \(F>0\), the nonempty set of maximizers has a minimum integer rank, and \(\mathrm{def:adaptive-rank-fiber-complexity}\) names such a certificate \(M^{\star}\).  This completes the proof.

For the smallest exact stress test, take \(n=1\), \(\Gamma_1=\{1\}\), and \(\mathcal S_1=\{\varnothing,\{1\}\}\).  The two retained characters span all functions on \(X_1=\{0,1\}\), so in evaluation coordinates \(K_1=[-1,1]^2\) and
\[
 \operatorname{vert}(K_1)=\{(-1,-1),(-1,1),(1,-1),(1,1)\}.
\]
There are the two assignments \(z=0,1\).  Program \((P)\) therefore has the three variables \((a_0,a_1,t)\), exactly \(1\cdot2^1+1\), and four listed constraints, exactly \(\lvert\operatorname{vert}(K_1)\rvert\).  For every fixed \((a_0,a_1)\), its risk is a convex quadratic on the square.  Expressing an arbitrary point of the square as the product mixture of its four corners and applying \((8)\) proves that none of the continuum of nonvertex schedules exceeds those four enumerated risks.  Thus exhaustive enumeration agrees with \((P)\) on the smallest nonconstant instance, including the variable and constraint counts.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every admissible fixed finite-population instance, the unrestricted and linear minimax risks obey the instance-adaptive certificate
\[
 \max\left\{\frac{F}{r_{\star}},m_{\mathrm{fib}}\right\}
 \le R^{\star}\le F=\mathcal D\le S_{\mathrm{fib}},
 \qquad
 \frac{F}{\kappa}\le R^{\star}\le F.                                            \tag{14}
\]
When \(F>0\), \(r_{\star}\) is the minimum rank of a dual optimizer; it has the stated value-one convention when \(F=0\).  The quantity \(\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\) is the effective number of assignment fibers carrying nonzero ambiguity.  When \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}>0\),
\[
 1\le\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}
 \le\left\lvert\{z\in\Omega_n:\rho_z>0\}\right\rvert
 \le2^n.
\]
When \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}=0\), all four values \(R^{\star},F,\mathcal D,S_{\mathrm{fib}}\) are zero.  The clipped incidence estimator has worst-case risk at most \(F\).  The factors in \((14)\) are instance dependent; no universal numerical comparison constant is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The declared lemma \(\mathrm{lem:rank-fiber-genuine-prior-certificates}\) supplies, for \(F>0\), a genuine prior with lower certificate \(F/r_{\star}\), and for every assignment fiber a genuine two-point prior with lower certificate at least \(p_\pi(z)\rho_z^2\).  Applying \(\mathrm{prop:primal-dual-certificates}\) to these priors gives
\[
 \max\left\{\frac{F}{r_{\star}},m_{\mathrm{fib}}\right\}\le R^{\star}.          \tag{15}
\]
The same lemma constructs, separately for every \(z\), a linear extension whose worst absolute error is \(\rho_z\); summing its squared errors with the design masses gives
\[
 F\le S_{\mathrm{fib}}.                                                           \tag{16}
\]
Moreover, \(\mathrm{prop:primal-dual-certificates}\) gives \(R^{\star}\le F\) and the clipped-estimator risk bound, while \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\) gives \(F=\mathcal D\).  Equations \((15)\) and \((16)\) establish the first chain in \((14)\).

When \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}>0\), the definition
\[
 \kappa=\min\{r_{\star},\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}=\frac{S_{\mathrm{fib}}}{m_{\mathrm{fib}}}
\]
allows two cases.  If \(\kappa=r_{\star}\), \((15)\) gives \(F/\kappa\le R^{\star}\).  If \(\kappa=\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\), then \((16)\) and the fiber lower bound give
\[
 \frac{F}{\kappa}
 \le\frac{S_{\mathrm{fib}}}{\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}}
 =m_{\mathrm{fib}}
 \le R^{\star}.
\]
The cardinality bound and the case \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}=0\), including the conclusion that every displayed risk is zero, are exactly the boundary conclusions of \(\mathrm{lem:rank-fiber-genuine-prior-certificates}\).  This proves every assertion and also makes explicit why the comparison factor is not dimension free.
added_lemmas.justification: The certificate quantifies the all-Borel value of the attainable linear risk through observable finite-instance rank and selector-fiber factors without asserting dimension-free equivalence.
added_lemmas.gap: ChenValiantValiant2020 leaves the universal comparison open; the proved conclusion is the exact unconditional comparison supplied by minimum dual rank and effective fiber count.
added_lemmas.consumer: Experimenters can report the incidence upper risk together with rank and fiber lower certificates that show how informative it is for unrestricted procedures.

added_lemmas.statement: As a rowwise corollary of the instance-adaptive risk certificate, let \(\mathfrak A\in\mathsf{Adm}\) and let \(r_n,\rho_{n,z},S_{n,\mathrm{fib}},m_{n,\mathrm{fib}},\kappa_{n,\mathrm{fib}}\), and \(\kappa_n\) be the quantities in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive-rank-fiber-complexity}\).  Then: \(\mathrm{(a)}\) \(F_n\to0\) implies \(R_n^{\star}\to0\); \(\mathrm{(b)}\) in every fixed row, \(R_n^{\star}=0\) if and only if \(F_n=0\); \(\mathrm{(c)}\) \(\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\to0\) implies \(F_n\to0\); and \(\mathrm{(d)}\) on every subfamily satisfying \(\sup_n\kappa_n<\infty\), one has \(R_n^{\star}\to0\) if and only if \(F_n\to0\).  Clause \(\mathrm{(d)}\) is conditional on that subfamily property and does not add a condition to \(\mathsf{Adm}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathfrak A\in\mathsf{Adm}\).  Applying \(\mathrm{thm:instance-adaptive-risk-certificate}\) to every row and using the rowwise definition of \(\kappa_n\) gives
\[
 0\le R_n^{\star}\le F_n\le\kappa_nR_n^{\star},
 \qquad n\ge1.                                                                    \tag{17}
\]
The factor \(\kappa_n\) is finite: if \(m_{n,\mathrm{fib}}=0\), it equals one by definition; otherwise the cardinality bound in the cited theorem gives \(\kappa_n\le\kappa_{n,\mathrm{fib}}\le2^n\).

If \(F_n\to0\), the first two inequalities in \((17)\) squeeze \(R_n^{\star}\) to zero, proving \(\mathrm{(a)}\).  In a fixed row, \(F_n=0\) implies \(R_n^{\star}=0\) by \(R_n^{\star}\le F_n\), while \(R_n^{\star}=0\) implies \(F_n=0\) by \(F_n\le\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\) and finiteness of \(\kappa_n\).  This proves \(\mathrm{(b)}\).

If \(\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\to0\), the last inequality in \((17)\) squeezes \(F_n\) to zero, proving \(\mathrm{(c)}\).  Finally, on a subfamily with \(C:=\sup_n\kappa_n<\infty\), \(R_n^{\star}\to0\) implies
\[
 0\le F_n\le\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\le C R_n^{\star}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{(a)}\), this proves the equivalence in \(\mathrm{(d)}\).  No reverse implication has been used or asserted when \(\kappa_n\) is unbounded.

payload.statement:
Fix a row \(n\).  For each \(i\in V_n\), let \(\mathcal V_i=\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\) and \(r_i=|\mathcal V_i|\).  Given the explicit local vertex tables \(\mathcal V_i\), the source masses \(p_{\pi}(z)\), and the computable arrays \(N_ze\) and \(\theta(e)\) for \(z\in\Omega_n\) and \(e\in\prod_{i\in V_n}\mathcal V_i\), the frontier is the exact finite convex quadratic epigraph program
\[
 F=\min_{\substack{a_z\in\mathbb R^{V_n},\ z\in\Omega_n\\ t\in\mathbb R}}t
 \quad\text{subject to}\quad
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)
 \bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_ze-\theta(e)\bigr)^2\le t
 \quad\text{for every }e\in\prod_{i\in V_n}\mathcal V_i.
\]
Before structural compression this program has exactly \(n2^n+1\) scalar decision variables and \(\prod_{i\in V_n}|\operatorname{vert}(K_i)|\) convex quadratic constraints.  Its minimum is attained, and its weight component may be chosen to be \(a^{\star}\).  Moreover, there exists \(\widetilde M^{\star}\in\mathfrak M(K)\), which may be chosen as the defined minimum-rank optimizer \(M^{\star}\) when \(F>0\), such that
\[
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)\psi_z(\widetilde M^{\star})
 =\mathcal D=F,
\]
so \(\widetilde M^{\star}\) is a matching moment certificate for the fully expanded primal program.
payload.proof_tex:
We first justify that the displayed lists are finite and exhaustive.  By \(\mathrm{def:local-evaluation-polytope}\), \(K_i\) is the intersection, inside the finite-dimensional space \(H_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{X_i}\), of the finitely many half-spaces
\[
 -1\le v_i(x)\le1,
 \qquad x\in X_i.
\]
It contains zero, is closed, and is bounded because the displayed inequalities bound every coordinate of the function \(v_i\) on the finite set \(X_i\).  Hence \(K_i\) is compact.  We give the finite-polytope argument explicitly.  At an extreme point, the active constraint functionals span the dual of \(H_i\): otherwise a nonzero direction annihilating every active functional could be added and subtracted with sufficiently small coefficient while all inactive strict inequalities remained satisfied, contradicting extremality.  One may therefore select \(\dim(H_i)\) linearly independent active constraints, whose equalities have at most one common solution.  There are only finitely many such selections, so the extreme-point set \(\mathcal V_i\) is finite.

Let \(C_i=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal V_i)\).  If some \(x\in K_i\) were outside \(C_i\), compactness of the finite convex hull would give a nearest point \(y\in C_i\).  With \(c=x-y\), minimality of \(y\) along each segment from \(y\) to \(u\in C_i\) gives
\[
 \langle c,u-y\rangle\le0,
 \qquad
 \langle c,x\rangle=\langle c,y\rangle+\|c\|^2
 >\sup_{u\in C_i}\langle c,u\rangle. \tag{0}
\]
The linear functional \(c\) attains its maximum on compact \(K_i\).  Its maximizer face contains an extreme point of \(K_i\): this follows by induction on affine dimension, because a non-singleton compact convex face admits a nonconstant linear functional whose maximizer face has strictly smaller affine dimension, while an extreme point of a face is extreme in the original set.  Call such an extreme maximizer \(e\).  Since \(x\in K_i\), \(\langle c,e\rangle\ge\langle c,x\rangle\), contradicting (0) because \(e\in\mathcal V_i\subseteq C_i\).  Thus
\[
 K_i=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal V_i),
 \qquad |\mathcal V_i|=r_i<\infty.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:bounded-fourier-class}\), \(K=\prod_{i\in V_n}K_i\).  We next prove
\[
 \operatorname{vert}(K)=\prod_{i\in V_n}\mathcal V_i. \tag{1}
\]
If one coordinate of a tuple in \(K\) is a nontrivial convex combination of two points of its factor, holding all other coordinates fixed gives a nontrivial convex decomposition of the tuple, so a product vertex must have vertex coordinates.  Conversely, if a tuple of coordinatewise vertices is a nontrivial convex combination of two points of \(K\), projection onto each coordinate expresses a vertex of \(K_i\) as the same convex combination; every pair of projected endpoints must therefore coincide with that vertex.  The two tuples coincide, proving (1).

For a fixed weight rule \(a=(a_z)_{z\in\Omega_n}\), define
\[
 Q_a(v)=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_{\pi}(z)
 \bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2.
\]
The masses \(p_{\pi}(z)\) are nonnegative by \(\mathrm{ass:source-product-design}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:source-overlap}\).  The map \(N_z\) is linear by \(\mathrm{def:observation-operator}\), and \(\theta\) is linear by its displayed formula in \(\mathrm{def:target-value}\), so each summand is the square of a linear functional of \(v\).  Therefore \(Q_a\) is convex.  Every \(v\in K\) is a convex combination \(v=\sum_e\lambda_e e\) of the vertices in (1), with \(\lambda_e\ge0\) and \(\sum_e\lambda_e=1\).  Convexity gives
\[
 Q_a(v)\le\sum_e\lambda_eQ_a(e)
 \le\max_{e\in\prod_i\mathcal V_i}Q_a(e).
\]
The reverse inequality after taking the supremum holds because every such \(e\) belongs to \(K\).  Consequently
\[
 \sup_{v\in K}Q_a(v)
 =\max_{e\in\prod_i\mathcal V_i}Q_a(e). \tag{2}
\]
Substituting (2) into \(\mathrm{def:linear-frontier}\) and introducing the epigraph variable \(t\) gives exactly the displayed program.  Each constraint is convex in the decision variables because it is a nonnegative weighted sum of squares of affine functions of the coordinates of \(a\).  There are \(|\Omega_n|=2^n\) vectors \(a_z\), each with \(n\) scalar coordinates, and one scalar \(t\), hence \(n2^n+1\) scalar variables.  Equation (1) gives exactly \(\prod_i r_i=\prod_i|\operatorname{vert}(K_i)|\) constraints.  The existence assertion in \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\) supplies a minimizing weight rule after the irrelevant directions \(\ker(N_z^{\ast})\) are quotiented out.  Pairing that rule with \(t=\max_eQ_a(e)\) proves attainment, and the weight component may be denoted by \(a^{\star}\).

It remains to verify that the equal-valued dual has an attained certificate, rather than merely the correct value.  The set \(K\) is compact by the preceding argument.  The map \(v\mapsto v\otimes v\) is continuous.  Let \(d\) be the dimension of the finite-dimensional vector space of self-adjoint operators on \(E\).  Every convex combination of more than \(d+1\) rank-one operators can be shortened: the participating operators are affinely dependent, so there are coefficients \(\alpha_k\), not all zero, with \(\sum_k\alpha_k=0\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k(v_k\otimes v_k)=0\); subtracting \(t\alpha_k\) from the original weights, where \(t=\min_{\alpha_k>0}\lambda_k/\alpha_k\), preserves the represented operator and total weight, leaves every weight nonnegative, and makes at least one weight zero.  Iteration gives a representation with at most \(d+1\) terms.  Thus \(\mathfrak M(K)\), as defined in \(\mathrm{def:moment-body}\), is the continuous image of the compact set consisting of the \(d\)-simplex times \(K^{d+1}\), and is compact.

For \(M\in\mathfrak M(K)\), \(z\in\Omega_n\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^{V_n}\), put
\[
 q_z(c;M)=
 \langle\ell-N_z^{\ast}c,M(\ell-N_z^{\ast}c)\rangle_E.
\]
Writing \(A=N_zMN_z^{\ast}\) and \(b=N_zM\ell\), expansion of the inner product yields
\[
 q_z(c;M)=\langle\ell,M\ell\rangle_E-2\langle c,b\rangle_{V_n}
 +\langle c,Ac\rangle_{V_n}.
\]
We now derive the required range condition.  If \(y\in\ker(A)\), then
\[
 0=\langle y,Ay\rangle_{V_n}
 =\langle N_z^{\ast}y,MN_z^{\ast}y\rangle_E.
\]
For a positive semidefinite self-adjoint operator \(M\), \(\langle u,Mu\rangle_E=0\) implies \(Mu=0\): for every \(f\in E\), nonnegativity of the quadratic polynomial \(\langle u+tf,M(u+tf)\rangle_E\) for all real \(t\), together with its zero constant term, forces \(\langle f,Mu\rangle_E=0\).  Applying this with \(u=N_z^{\ast}y\) gives \(MN_z^{\ast}y=0\), and hence
\[
 \langle y,b\rangle_{V_n}
 =\langle N_z^{\ast}y,M\ell\rangle_E=0.
\]
Thus \(b\perp\ker(A)\).  Since \(A\) is self-adjoint on finite-dimensional Euclidean space, \(\operatorname{range}(A)=(\ker A)^{\perp}\), so \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\).  Hence \(AA^{\dagger}b=b\), and direct completion of the square gives
\[
 q_z(c;M)=\psi_z(M)
 +\langle c-A^{\dagger}b,A(c-A^{\dagger}b)\rangle_{V_n}.
\]
Because \(A\) is positive semidefinite, the last term is nonnegative and vanishes at \(c=A^{\dagger}b\).  Therefore
\[
 \psi_z(M)=\min_{c\in\mathbb R^{V_n}}q_z(c;M). \tag{3}
\]
For fixed \(c\), the map \(M\mapsto q_z(c;M)\) is continuous and affine.  Equation (3) makes \(\psi_z\) a pointwise infimum of continuous functions, hence upper semicontinuous: if \(M_k\to M\), then for every fixed \(c\),
\[
 \limsup_k\psi_z(M_k)
 \le\lim_k q_z(c;M_k)=q_z(c;M),
\]
and taking the infimum over \(c\) gives \(\limsup_k\psi_z(M_k)\le\psi_z(M)\).  The finite nonnegative weighted sum \(M\mapsto\sum_zp_{\pi}(z)\psi_z(M)\) is therefore upper semicontinuous.  A maximizing sequence in compact \(\mathfrak M(K)\) has a convergent subsequence, and upper semicontinuity shows that its limit \(\widetilde M^{\star}\) attains the maximum.  When \(F>0\), the nonempty maximizer set contains a member of minimum rank because rank takes values in the finite set \(\{0,\ldots,\dim(E)\}\); this member is the defined \(M^{\star}\), so \(\widetilde M^{\star}\) may be chosen as \(M^{\star}\).  Finally, \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\) identifies that attained value with \(\mathcal D\), while \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\) proves \(F=\mathcal D\).  This yields the asserted matching certificate.

For every admissible fixed instance, write \(\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\) for the vertex set of the local polytope \(K_i\).  The exact linear frontier is the finite convex epigraph program
\[
\begin{aligned}
 F={}&\min_{\substack{t\in\mathbb R\\ a\in(\mathbb R^{V_n})^{\Omega_n}}}t\\
 \text{subject to }{}&
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \left[
 \sum_{i\in V_n}(a_z)_i v_i(z_{\Gamma_i})
 -\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)v_i(x)
 \right]^2\le t
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\prod_{i\in V_n}\operatorname{vert}(K_i).
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{P}
\]
Its explicit numeric inputs are the tables \(p_\pi(z)\), \(p_{\pi',i}(x)\), the restrictions \(z_{\Gamma_i}\), and the vertex-evaluation tables \(\{(v_i(x))_{x\in X_i}:v_i\in\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\}\), all computed from the known \(\pi,\pi',\Gamma_i,\mathcal S_i\).  Program \((P)\) has exactly \(n2^n+1\) real decision variables and \(\prod_{i\in V_n}\lvert\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\rvert\) listed convex quadratic constraints.  An optimum exists, its weight component may be taken to be \(a^{\star}\), and there is a matching moment certificate \(M\in\mathfrak M(K)\) such that
\[
 F=\mathcal D=
 \sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)\psi_z(M).                                         \tag{D}
\]
When \(F>0\), \(M\) may be chosen to be the minimum-rank optimizer \(M^{\star}\) from \(\mathrm{def:adaptive-rank-fiber-complexity}\).
payload.proof_tex:
For a fixed weight array \(a\), put
\[
 Q_a(v)=\sum_{z\in\Omega_n}p_\pi(z)
 \bigl(a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)\bigr)^2.
\]
Each residual in this sum is linear in \(v\).  Since \(s\mapsto s^2\) is convex and the design masses are nonnegative, for \(v,w\in K\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\),
\[
 Q_a(\lambda v+(1-\lambda)w)
 \le \lambda Q_a(v)+(1-\lambda)Q_a(w).                                           \tag{8}
\]

We next justify the vertex reduction rather than assume it.  By \(\mathrm{def:local-evaluation-polytope}\), \(K_i\) is the intersection of the finite-dimensional space \(H_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{X_i}\) with the finitely many slabs \(-1\le h(x)\le1\), \(x\in X_i\).  It contains zero, is closed, and is bounded in the evaluation coordinates; hence it is a nonempty compact polytope.  Every point of such a polytope is a convex combination of its vertices: indeed, induct on the dimension of the point's smallest face.  A zero-dimensional face is a vertex.  In a positive-dimensional smallest face, a line through the point in a nonzero direction of the face meets the compact face in a closed segment with two boundary endpoints; the point is a convex combination of those endpoints, and each endpoint has a smallest face of strictly smaller dimension.  The induction terminates because the dimension is finite.  This also shows that the vertex set is finite, since every vertex is the unique solution of a full-rank subsystem selected from finitely many defining equalities.

Thus write each \(v_i\in K_i\) as \(v_i=\sum_{k_i}\lambda_{i,k_i}u_{i,k_i}\), where \(u_{i,k_i}\in\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\), \(\lambda_{i,k_i}\ge0\), and \(\sum_{k_i}\lambda_{i,k_i}=1\).  Expanding the product gives
\[
 v=\sum_{(k_i)_{i\in V_n}}
 \left(\prod_{i\in V_n}\lambda_{i,k_i}\right)
 (u_{i,k_i})_{i\in V_n},                                                         \tag{9}
\]
a convex combination of the product vertices.  Applying the two-point convexity inequality \((8)\) repeatedly to the finite combination \((9)\) yields
\[
 \sup_{v\in K}Q_a(v)
 =\max_{v\in\prod_i\operatorname{vert}(K_i)}Q_a(v).                              \tag{10}
\]
The left-to-right inequality in \((10)\) follows from the convex combination; the reverse inequality follows because every listed product vertex belongs to \(K\).

By \(\mathrm{def:observation-operator}\) and \(\mathrm{def:target-value}\), the residual at a product vertex is exactly
\[
 a_z^{\mathsf T}N_zv-\theta(v)
 =\sum_{i\in V_n}(a_z)_iv_i(z_{\Gamma_i})
 -\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\sum_{x\in X_i}p_{\pi',i}(x)v_i(x).                    \tag{11}
\]
Substituting \((10)\) and \((11)\) into \(\mathrm{def:linear-frontier}\) gives precisely the epigraph program \((P)\).  There are \(2^n\) vectors \(a_z\in\mathbb R^{V_n}\) and one scalar \(t\), hence \(n2^n+1\) real variables.  Equation \((10)\) supplies one listed constraint for each element of \(\prod_i\operatorname{vert}(K_i)\), hence the claimed product count.  Each constraint is a nonnegative weighted sum of squares of affine functions of \(a\), bounded above by the affine variable \(t\); it is therefore convex quadratic.  The input list in the statement is exactly the list of coefficients occurring in \((11)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\), the infimum over \(a\) is attained, so the epigraph optimum is attained with \(t=F\) and weight component \(a^{\star}\).

It remains to certify the matching dual optimizer.  For \(M\in\mathfrak M(K)\), the range condition in \(\mathrm{def:moment-dual}\) and completion of the positive-semidefinite quadratic give, for every \(z\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \psi_z(M)
 &=\min_{b\in\mathbb R^{V_n}}
 \langle\ell-N_z^{\ast}b,\,M(\ell-N_z^{\ast}b)\rangle_E.
\end{aligned}                                                                     \tag{12}
\]
To check \((12)\), expand the right side as
\[
 \langle\ell,M\ell\rangle_E
 -2\langle b,N_zM\ell\rangle_{V_n}
 +\langle b,(N_zMN_z^{\ast})b\rangle_{V_n}.
\]
Because \(N_zM\ell\) lies in the range of \(N_zMN_z^{\ast}\), its minimizers solve the normal equation and the minimum is
\[
 \langle\ell,M\ell\rangle_E
 -\left\langle N_zM\ell,
 (N_zMN_z^{\ast})^{\dagger}N_zM\ell\right\rangle_{V_n},
\]
which is the defining formula for \(\psi_z(M)\).

Independence of the finitely many coordinates \(b_z\) in \((12)\) implies
\[
 \Phi(M):=\sum_zp_\pi(z)\psi_z(M)
 =\inf_{a}\sum_zp_\pi(z)

payload.statement: As a rowwise corollary of the instance-adaptive risk certificate, let \(\mathfrak A\in\mathsf{Adm}\) and let \(r_n,\rho_{n,z},S_{n,\mathrm{fib}},m_{n,\mathrm{fib}},\kappa_{n,\mathrm{fib}}\), and \(\kappa_n\) be the quantities in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive-rank-fiber-complexity}\).  Then: \(\mathrm{(a)}\) \(F_n\to0\) implies \(R_n^{\star}\to0\); \(\mathrm{(b)}\) in every fixed row, \(R_n^{\star}=0\) if and only if \(F_n=0\); \(\mathrm{(c)}\) \(\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\to0\) implies \(F_n\to0\); and \(\mathrm{(d)}\) on every subfamily satisfying \(\sup_n\kappa_n<\infty\), one has \(R_n^{\star}\to0\) if and only if \(F_n\to0\). payload.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathfrak A\in\mathsf{Adm}\).  Applying \(\mathrm{thm:instance-adaptive-risk-certificate}\) to every row and using the rowwise definition of \(\kappa_n\) gives
\[
 0\le R_n^{\star}\le F_n\le\kappa_nR_n^{\star},
 \qquad n\ge1.                                                                    \tag{17}
\]
The factor \(\kappa_n\) is finite: if \(m_{n,\mathrm{fib}}=0\), it equals one by definition; otherwise the cardinality bound in the cited theorem gives \(\kappa_n\le\kappa_{n,\mathrm{fib}}\le2^n\).

If \(F_n\to0\), the first two inequalities in \((17)\) squeeze \(R_n^{\star}\) to zero, proving \(\mathrm{(a)}\).  In a fixed row, \(F_n=0\) implies \(R_n^{\star}=0\) by \(R_n^{\star}\le F_n\), while \(R_n^{\star}=0\) implies \(F_n=0\) by \(F_n\le\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\) and finiteness of \(\kappa_n\).  This proves \(\mathrm{(b)}\).

If \(\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\to0\), the last inequality in \((17)\) squeezes \(F_n\) to zero, proving \(\mathrm{(c)}\).  Finally, on a subfamily with \(C:=\sup_n\kappa_n<\infty\), \(R_n^{\star}\to0\) implies
\[
 0\le F_n\le\kappa_nR_n^{\star}\le C R_n^{\star}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{(a)}\), this proves the equivalence in \(\mathrm{(d)}\).  No reverse implication has been used or asserted when \(\kappa_n\) is unbounded.

payload.statement:
For every admissible fixed finite-population instance, the unrestricted and linear minimax risks obey the instance-adaptive certificate
\[
 \max\left\{\frac{F}{r_{\star}},m_{\mathrm{fib}}\right\}
 \le R^{\star}\le F=\mathcal D\le S_{\mathrm{fib}},
 \qquad
 \frac{F}{\kappa}\le R^{\star}\le F.                                            \tag{14}
\]
When \(F>0\), \(r_{\star}\) is the minimum rank of a dual optimizer; it has the stated value-one convention when \(F=0\).  The quantity \(\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\) is the effective number of assignment fibers carrying nonzero ambiguity.  When \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}>0\),
\[
 1\le\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}
 \le\left\lvert\{z\in\Omega_n:\rho_z>0\}\right\rvert
 \le2^n.
\]
When \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}=0\), all four values \(R^{\star},F,\mathcal D,S_{\mathrm{fib}}\) are zero.  The clipped incidence estimator has worst-case risk at most \(F\).  The factors in \((14)\) are instance dependent; no universal numerical comparison constant is asserted.
payload.proof_tex:
The declared lemma \(\mathrm{lem:rank-fiber-genuine-prior-certificates}\) supplies, for \(F>0\), a genuine prior with lower certificate \(F/r_{\star}\), and for every assignment fiber a genuine two-point prior with lower certificate at least \(p_\pi(z)\rho_z^2\).  Applying \(\mathrm{prop:primal-dual-certificates}\) to these priors gives
\[
 \max\left\{\frac{F}{r_{\star}},m_{\mathrm{fib}}\right\}\le R^{\star}.          \tag{15}
\]
The same lemma constructs, separately for every \(z\), a linear extension whose worst absolute error is \(\rho_z\); summing its squared errors with the design masses gives
\[
 F\le S_{\mathrm{fib}}.                                                           \tag{16}
\]
Moreover, \(\mathrm{prop:primal-dual-certificates}\) gives \(R^{\star}\le F\) and the clipped-estimator risk bound, while \(\mathrm{lem:selector-reduction-and-dual}\) gives \(F=\mathcal D\).  Equations \((15)\) and \((16)\) establish the first chain in \((14)\).

When \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}>0\), the definition
\[
 \kappa=\min\{r_{\star},\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}=\frac{S_{\mathrm{fib}}}{m_{\mathrm{fib}}}
\]
allows two cases.  If \(\kappa=r_{\star}\), \((15)\) gives \(F/\kappa\le R^{\star}\).  If \(\kappa=\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}\), then \((16)\) and the fiber lower bound give
\[
 \frac{F}{\kappa}
 \le\frac{S_{\mathrm{fib}}}{\kappa_{\mathrm{fib}}}
 =m_{\mathrm{fib}}
 \le R^{\star}.
\]
The cardinality bound and the case \(m_{\mathrm{fib}}=0\), including the conclusion that every displayed risk is zero, are exactly the boundary conclusions of \(\mathrm{lem:rank-fiber-genuine-prior-certificates}\).  This proves every assertion and also makes explicit why the comparison factor is not dimension free.
